AAPL.inst_own_summary: 73.6% institutional ownership per GuruFocus (Jun 2026); other trackers (Yahoo/SimplyWallSt) show low-60s% for late 2025, with methodology differences explaining the spread rather than a real swing.
AAPL.moat_summary: Morningstar rates Apple Wide moat/Stable trend, driven by switching costs and network effects across 2.2B+ active devices; the one flagged risk is AI (Siri/Apple Intelligence) falling behind Gemini/GPT by 2027.

ABBV.inst_own_summary: 70.23% institutional as of Oct 2025, down from the 73-74% range reported earlier in 2025.
ABBV.moat_summary: Humira revenue fell 40% YoY (Q1 2026) on biosimilar competition, but Skyrizi and Rinvoq have more than offset ~$16B of Humira erosion, driving record 2025 sales of $61.1B (+8.6%).

ABNB.inst_own_summary: MarketBeat-cited figure of about 80.8% (other sources show 41-57% depending on method, and founders hold large insider stakes); institutions sold 273.8M shares versus 184.9M bought last quarter per Fintel.
ABNB.moat_summary: A two-sided marketplace with 5M+ hosts, 2B+ guest arrivals and about 90% direct traffic is a strong network moat, but Booking.com and Vrbo now match vacation-rental features.

ABT.inst_own_summary: ~80% institutional per multiple Simply Wall St-sourced Yahoo Finance articles (mid-2025); one outlier source cites 58.7%, likely a different ownership-base methodology.
ABT.moat_summary: Morningstar assigns Abbott a Narrow moat (not Wide) resting on its product portfolio breadth; the company still lags peers on profitability margins despite operating in attractive device/diagnostics niches.

ADBE.inst_own_summary: Institutions held 79.9% at Dec 2025 (down from 81.2%); 1,163 funds cut vs 1,059 added, though aggregate shares rose 3.56M; BlackRock holds 9.56%.
ADBE.moat_summary: Proprietary formats (.psd, .ai) and workflow lock-in give ~70%+ share in core creative categories (GuruFocus moat 9/10), but Canva, Figma and generative AI are pressuring growth and margins.

ADI.inst_own_summary: 85.9% institutional as of Dec 2025, down notably from 93.1% in Sept 2025; BlackRock is the top holder at ~8.68%.
ADI.moat_summary: ADI holds >40% share in high-performance data converters/amplifiers and is the #2 analog chipmaker behind TI, using a focused premium-pricing niche strategy rather than competing across the full spectrum.

ALL.inst_own_summary: Institutions hold roughly 80% of Allstate across 1,723 13D/G/13F filers holding 210.7M shares; recent-quarter net direction not found.
ALL.moat_summary: Real but limited moat from brand, scale in personal lines and agent distribution, but a higher-cost agent-centric model lags Progressive and GEICO in direct and data analytics.

ALNY.inst_own_summary: Fintel shows about 93% institutional ownership across 1,536 holders; past 12 months had 417 buyers vs 253 sellers with $6.05B inflows vs $5.28B outflows.
ALNY.moat_summary: Morningstar assigns a narrow moat: RNAi/GalNAc platform and subcutaneous quarterly Amvuttra are differentiated, but BridgeBio's Attruby and Pfizer's Vyndaqel compete hard in ATTR.

AMAT.inst_own_summary: 79.0% institutional as of March 2026, down from 82.1% the prior quarter.
AMAT.moat_summary: Wide moat from equipment switching costs remains intact at leading-edge nodes (2nm/3nm, HBM, hybrid bonding), but China export controls are cutting China revenue share from ~40% to the mid-20s% and six domestic Chinese equipment makers grew combined sales 10x from 2020-2025.

AMD.inst_own_summary: 71.34% institutional as of Oct 24, 2025 per 13F data; BlackRock is the largest holder (~$29.6B position as of Mar 2026 13F).
AMD.moat_summary: AMD's AI GPU share has stayed stuck at roughly 5-7% vs. Nvidia's ~80% and essentially unchanged over the past 12 months; Nvidia's CUDA software lock-in still holds despite AMD's ROCm and MI350X hardware parity claims.

AME.inst_own_summary: MarketBeat shows 87.43% institutional ownership, with 666 buyers vs 489 sellers over 12 months and $8.37B inflows vs $4.97B outflows.
AME.moat_summary: Morningstar rates it wide moat: products designed into customer platforms in thousands of niche applications create re-qualification and certification switching costs, reinforced by serial niche acquisitions.

AMGN.inst_own_summary: 81% institutional per Yahoo/Simply Wall St data (Nov 2025); other trackers show 71.7%-79% depending on methodology.
AMGN.moat_summary: Wide moat maintained as Repatha and a strengthening pipeline offset accelerating biosimilar erosion on Prolia/Xgeva, which intensified through 2026; FY2026 revenue guidance was raised to $38.8B.

AMZN.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership commonly cited in the 65-75% range for late 2025 (72.2% per one tracker); figures vary by source/date.
AMZN.moat_summary: Morningstar rates AWS/retail/ads all Wide moat; AWS holds ~29-30% global cloud share, still #1 but growing slower than Azure (20% share) in percentage terms.

ANET.inst_own_summary: 82.47% institutional as of Sept 2025, up from 68.79%-70% reported earlier in 2025.
ANET.moat_summary: Arista's investor presentation shows 'strong, sustained share gains' vs. Cisco in high-speed (100G-800G) data center switching through 2025, with EOS software lock-in as the key differentiator; NVIDIA entering Ethernet via InfiniBand is the main named future risk.

APH.inst_own_summary: 94.84% institutional, 0.52% insiders, 4.64% retail; Vanguard is the largest holder at 11.51%.
APH.moat_summary: GuruFocus Moat Score of 7/10 (entry-level wide moat); components requiring military/AEC-Q automotive certification get 'spec'd in' for a platform's entire 5-15 year production life, and revenue grew 51.7% YoY, reflecting continued share gains via its acquisition-driven strategy.

ARM.inst_own_summary: 13F-reported institutional ownership is only ~7.5% because SoftBank Group holds ~86% of ARM as a controlling insider, leaving a small float for institutions/retail.
ARM.moat_summary: Arm's ISA licensing model underpins chips in over 99% of smartphones with 22M+ developers building on the architecture, creating a two-sided network effect and high switching costs that make its IP moat hard to dislodge.

ASML.inst_own_summary: 14.8% institutional (US 13F filers) as of Dec 2025, down from 15.4% in Sept 2025 -- reflects only US-registered institutional filers against ASML's NASDAQ-listed shares, not global ownership, since ASML's primary listing is Euronext Amsterdam; not a controlling-insider situation.
ASML.moat_summary: ASML is the sole global supplier of EUV lithography systems; Morningstar rates it Wide moat, noting rivals would need decades of R&D and tens of billions in investment to replicate the technology, and TSMC/Intel/Samsung fabs are already redesigned around it.

AVGO.inst_own_summary: 77.15% institutional as of May 24, 2026 per GuruFocus, up from the 71.9-73.3% range reported for Sept-Dec 2025.
AVGO.moat_summary: Broadcom holds ~70% share of the custom AI ASIC market with deals across Alphabet, Meta, Anthropic and OpenAI, but MediaTek is targeting 15-20% of an estimated $80B custom AI-chip market by 2027, and hyperscaler in-house chip development is the named longer-term risk.

AXON.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership about 88% by Q4 2025; in Q2 2026 246 institutions opened new positions vs 128 closed among 1,181 holders.
AXON.moat_summary: GuruFocus moat score 7: integrated TASER/body-cam/cloud evidence software ecosystem with high switching costs, though Motorola's $1.5B D-Fend deal signals rising public-safety tech competition.

AXP.inst_own_summary: Sources disagreed unusually widely (41.5% to 84.3%) depending on methodology; 66% (Feb 2025, Simply Wall St/Yahoo) is used as the most consistent figure relative to comparable tickers, but treat with caution.
AXP.moat_summary: Amex's closed-loop network lets it capture the full economics of a swipe (issuing + acquiring + network) unlike open-loop Visa/Mastercard-based issuers, and card fee revenue grew 18% YoY in Q1 2026, decoupling profitability from cyclical spend.

BA.inst_own_summary: Institutions hold about 73% of Boeing shares (2,784 holders, ~572.2M shares) as of late April 2026; Vanguard and BlackRock are the largest holders.
BA.moat_summary: Boeing's 737 MAX now holds only ~40% of the global narrowbody market vs. the Airbus A320neo family's ~60%, and the A321neo gives Airbus a range/efficiency edge; the Boeing-Airbus duopoly still provides residual pricing power but Boeing keeps ceding narrowbody share.

BAC.inst_own_summary: 72.1% institutional as of Dec 2025, down from 74.4% in Sept 2025; Vanguard is the top holder at 8.54%.
BAC.moat_summary: Wide moat from #1 US retail deposit share (~$298B lead over next competitor) and lowest industry cost of deposits, but Morningstar and independent analysts flag fintech (SoFi, etc.) encroachment on deposits/payments as an active erosion risk -- moat is 'durable but not impermeable.'

BKNG.inst_own_summary: 91.20% institutional / 0.18% insider / 8.62% retail; one Dec 2025 source cited a higher ~96% figure.
BKNG.moat_summary: Morningstar upgraded Booking to Wide moat from Narrow in 2025 on network strength and AI positioning, but shares fell ~10% in 2026 on fears that Meta's 'Muse' AI shopping agent and Google's own AI search could disintermediate OTA platforms -- a live, named threat.

BKR.inst_own_summary: MarketBeat shows institutions holding 92.06% of BKR; Fintel counts 1,161 institutional holders led by Vanguard, BlackRock and State Street, but no clear recent-quarter net flow was found.
BKR.moat_summary: The IET segment makes the heavy turbomachinery for the LNG buildout that SLB and Halliburton do not, and hardware plus software/IP create high switching costs (ROIC about 3.7 points above WACC).

BLK.inst_own_summary: 84.54% institutional as of Q4 2025 (3,530 institutions holding 129.03M shares), up from 79.31% in Sept 2025; one outlier source cited 44.53%, likely a different denominator.
BLK.moat_summary: Aladdin's risk-analytics platform creates high switching costs for institutional clients, and iShares' 1,600+ ETF lineup plus BlackRock/Vanguard/State Street's ~74% combined US equity ETF market share reinforces a scale-driven network effect.

BMY.inst_own_summary: 81% institutional per a May 2025 source; other 2025 figures ranged 77-78%, and BMY's own 10-K/proxy puts it above 70%.
BMY.moat_summary: Facing a ~$30B patent cliff through 2026, but the Growth Portfolio (Mirati/RayzeBio/Karuna deals) now generates 55% of revenue and grew 12% YoY in Q1 2026, overtaking the declining Legacy Portfolio (-6%) -- a successful but still in-progress transition.

BNY.inst_own_summary: Institutions and hedge funds hold about 85.31% (Vanguard largest at 9.9%); Aug 2026 13Fs show new stakes such as Primecap's $376.5M, but a full quarterly net figure was not found and some filers trimmed.
BNY.moat_summary: World's largest custodian with over $62 trillion in assets under custody/administration; embedded back-office infrastructure creates high switching costs and sticky fee revenue.

BRK-B.inst_own_summary: 65.10% institutional / 5.55% insider / 29.35% retail per WallStreetZen; other sources cite figures as low as 43%, likely reflecting Class A/B share differences and Buffett-family-linked holdings, which act as a partial controlling-insider stake.
BRK-B.moat_summary: Morningstar cut Berkshire's rating to Narrow moat/Low uncertainty in 2026, explicitly citing that the capital-allocation edge which historically justified a Wide rating 'has gotten thinner over the years' and is expected to weaken further under new CEO Greg Abel.

BSX.inst_own_summary: Fintel-tracked institutional ownership is about 89.07% (GuruFocus shows 100.05%); 12-month inflows of $17.66B (1,245 buyers) versus $11.73B outflows (768 sellers).
BSX.moat_summary: Morningstar says the moat remains intact in 2026 (clinical data, regulatory barriers, physician training, product breadth) despite slower PFA growth and a Watchman slowdown with new competition.

BX.inst_own_summary: 71.65% institutional / 1.05% insider / 27.30% retail; Vanguard is the top holder at 9.18%.
BX.moat_summary: Blackstone's $1.3T AUM and proprietary deal-sourcing data (270+ portfolio companies, 13,000 real estate assets, 5,000 lending relationships) support a scale moat, with $213.3B in dry powder as of Q1 2026 giving it an edge in sourcing quality deals.

C.inst_own_summary: 82% institutional as of Nov 2025, up from 74% in Feb 2025.
C.moat_summary: Morningstar explicitly rates Citigroup 'no-moat,' noting wealth/card markets remain highly competitive and Citi isn't building retail scale to rival peers, despite strength in its institutional cross-border payments network (94-country local clearing licenses).

CAT.inst_own_summary: 71.85% institutional / 1.13% insider / 27.02% retail per WallStreetZen; a second source cited 69.01%.
CAT.moat_summary: Morningstar rates Caterpillar Wide moat on ~20% market share across key products, 20,000+ patents, and dealer-network switching costs, but flags directly in its own headline that 'competition escalates' as a live dynamic to watch.

CB.inst_own_summary: About 83.8% institutional as of mid-Sept 2026, down from ~90.8% reported in March 2026 (sources vary in methodology/date).
CB.moat_summary: Morningstar calls Chubb a 'moaty' global insurer post ACE-Chubb merger — one of few insurers with the global footprint to service multinational corporate clients, creating a real barrier to entry for smaller rivals.

CDNS.inst_own_summary: Fintel shows 84.85% institutional ownership (236.7M shares); trailing 12 months had 1,000 buyers ($12.61B inflows) versus 661 sellers ($8.95B outflows).
CDNS.moat_summary: EDA duopoly with Synopsys plus foundry-certified flows and multi-year subscriptions create high switching costs; Cadence added Hexagon's Design & Engineering unit ($3.16B, Feb 2026) to extend into system simulation.

CEG.inst_own_summary: Institutions own about 82.6% (1,841 holders, Q1 2026 13Fs); Q1 saw 311 full exits and 1,326 trims versus 214 new positions and 293 adds, with Q2 tracked-fund holdings down 16.8%.
CEG.moat_summary: Largest US nuclear fleet is hard to replicate given regulatory and cost barriers, but GuruFocus scores it 6 (narrow moat) and it lacks brand or proprietary technology edge.

CI.inst_own_summary: MarketBeat-derived reports cite 86.99% institutional ownership with new stakes such as GQG Partners in Q2 and adds by small holders; aggregate net flow not clearly found (some quoted CalSTRS figures look like data errors and were ignored).
CI.moat_summary: Narrow moat from Express Scripts scale (over a billion prescriptions a year) and sticky large-employer relationships, but weak Medicare Advantage presence and competition from UnitedHealth's Optum.

CL.inst_own_summary: Institutions own about 80.4% (Vanguard 9.7%, BlackRock 8.2%, State Street 5.8%); latest 13F cycle had 331 adding vs 387 trimming.
CL.moat_summary: Dominant global oral-care position (roughly 40% toothpaste share cited, 2.5x nearest rival) with presence in over half of households; risk is category concentration and slow growth.

CME.inst_own_summary: Fintel shows 87.75% institutional ownership; 1,176 buyers ($16.47B inflows) vs 798 sellers ($10.44B outflows) over 12 months.
CME.moat_summary: Futures liquidity network effect plus integrated clearing and DTCC cross-margining create high barriers versus ICE and Nasdaq.

COP.inst_own_summary: 83.9% institutional; trailing-12-month 13F activity shows 1,801 institutional buyers vs 1,264 sellers and $20.1B inflows vs $8.9B outflows, a clear net-buying trend.
COP.moat_summary: GuruFocus moat score of 7/10 (entry-level wide moat) driven by ~15B boe of Lower-48/Permian resource inventory with sub-$40/bbl WTI breakeven cost — a structural low-cost asset advantage over less-efficient producers.

COST.inst_own_summary: 69% institutional (Vanguard 9.4%, BlackRock 7.6%, State Street 4.1% are largest holders); no clear recent buy/sell trend surfaced.
COST.moat_summary: Morningstar wide-moat rating: Costco holds over 60% share of the US warehouse-club market and ~90% membership renewal rates, with membership fees (not merchandise margin) funding the bulk of operating profit — a structurally hard-to-replicate model.

CPRT.inst_own_summary: Institutions held 80.7% as of Sept 2025 (down from 82.9% in June), with institutional shares down 6.9M QoQ though more filers added (541) than trimmed (433); Vanguard holds 11.27%.
CPRT.moat_summary: Zoning-constrained salvage yard footprint plus a two-sided online auction where international buyers take ~40% of US vehicles sold gives wide-moat scale, though analysts flag fee-rate competitive pressure and a fiscal Q2 2026 miss.

CRM.inst_own_summary: 80.4% institutional per recent aggregated data; no explicit recent 13F buy/sell trend found (stock itself is down ~42.5% off highs on AI-related growth concerns, which is a price move, not a confirmed ownership-trend datapoint).
CRM.moat_summary: Seat-based pricing model is directly threatened by AI agents (Agentforce and rivals) that let customers cut human-license headcount; revenue growth of 8.4% is lagging peers as value shifts up the AI stack toward foundation-model and hardware providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia).

CRWD.inst_own_summary: 70.9% institutional as of May 2026 (other trackers show 60-74% depending on date/methodology); no clear directional trend confirmed.
CRWD.moat_summary: Leads endpoint protection with 22.7% market share and a widening data moat (5T+ security events/day across 29,000+ customers via Falcon Flex), but faces real pricing pressure from Microsoft bundling Defender into E3/E5 licenses and SentinelOne crossing $1B ARR.

CRWV.inst_own_summary: About 55.6% institutionally held (founders and insiders hold large stakes); Vanguard raised its position 109.67% and Viking doubled, while Citadel cut 39% and Deutsche Bank cut 45%.
CRWV.moat_summary: GuruFocus scores the moat only 2, but Nvidia partner access to Blackwell/Rubin, a 250,000+ GPU fleet and a roughly $104B contracted backlog are building a scale advantage against hyperscalers.

CSCO.inst_own_summary: 76.6% institutional as of May 2026 (one other source cites ~83%); no clear recent trend confirmed.
CSCO.moat_summary: Morningstar rates Cisco wide-moat on dominant switching/routing/wireless-access share plus high switching costs; fiscal 2026 AI infrastructure revenue guidance was raised to $4B (from $3B) as networking becomes a bottleneck/enabler for AI buildouts.

CTAS.inst_own_summary: MarketBeat-style figure of 63.46% institutional ownership (lower than peers) across 2,391 holders; Vanguard added 1.3% in Q1 and BlackRock opened a large Q2 position.
CTAS.moat_summary: Morningstar wide moat strengthening: route density, 90%+ retention and bundled uniforms/mats/safety products lift revenue per stop, with ROIC around 27%.

CVX.inst_own_summary: ~67% institutional per Yahoo/early-2026 data; other trackers show a wide 54-74% range depending on methodology, so treat this as an approximate midpoint rather than a precise figure.
CVX.moat_summary: Analysis flags ROIC running below WACC and a sharply declining profitability trend from 2021-2025 despite scale advantages; management is targeting $3-4B of structural cost savings by end-2026 specifically to try to offset the erosion.

D.inst_own_summary: About 79% institutionally owned (May 2026 data; other sources 72-84%), led by BlackRock at 9.2%; recent-quarter net 13F flow direction not found.
D.moat_summary: Morningstar cut Dominion to a narrow moat from wide in 2023 after expected divestiture of contracted nonutility assets, leaving regulated Virginia/Carolinas monopoly utilities as the core, with rising Virginia political and regulatory pressure.

DAL.inst_own_summary: Sources conflict (roughly 44% to 79% depending on provider and date) and no reliable recent-quarter 13F net change was found, so no figure is recorded.
DAL.moat_summary: Best-in-class operational reliability plus premium and loyalty revenue (61% of total, $8.2B from the Amex SkyMiles co-brand in FY2025 targeting $10B by 2029) support pricing power, though airlines remain cyclical and fuel-exposed.

DASH.inst_own_summary: About 90.6% institutionally owned across 1,097 holders; last quarter institutions bought 283.8M shares and sold 295.7M, roughly flat, though 12-month inflows ($14.75B) far exceed outflows ($7.65B).
DASH.moat_summary: Roughly 56% US delivery share with network effects and DashPass subscribers, but low switching costs and Uber Eats (23%) force ongoing promo spend, so analysts call it a narrow/moderate moat.

DDOG.inst_own_summary: Institutions own roughly 76-78% of DDOG (78.29% cited; 1,110 holders); recent-quarter net buying vs selling not detailed in results.
DDOG.moat_summary: Switching costs from embedded dashboards/runbooks, 1,000+ integrations and a unified telemetry data model, with hyperscalers replacing in-house tools; main threat is bundled hyperscaler observability.

DE.inst_own_summary: Institutions own roughly 71-74% of Deere shares across multiple 2025/2026 reports (figures vary by source/date).
DE.moat_summary: Deere's precision-ag software stack (1M+ connected machines, 500M engaged acres) creates switching costs and an estimated 3-5 year technology gap over CNH Industrial and AGCO in autonomy/crop analytics, reinforced by a 2,200+ dealer network.

DELL.inst_own_summary: 38.2% institutional — unusually low because founder/CEO Michael Dell personally and via trust controls roughly 46-52% of shares (figures vary by source/date after recent insider sales), leaving less of the float for institutions.
DELL.moat_summary: AI-centric server revenue grew 422% YoY in Q1 2026 and Dell is approaching roughly half of the OEM AI server/systems market with #1 share in AI-centric storage, though HPE and Supermicro are adding competing full-rack solutions.

DHR.inst_own_summary: 82.4% institutional per GuruFocus (other sources show ~79%); no clear recent buy/sell trend confirmed.
DHR.moat_summary: Bioprocessing orders returned to mid-teens growth in Q2 2026 ('early innings' of a multi-year capex cycle per management); moat rests on workflow lock-in in diagnostics/bioprocessing where validation is slow and switching is costly.

DIS.inst_own_summary: 76.8% institutional in June 2026, up from 74.1% in March 2026.
DIS.moat_summary: ESPN/linear-TV moat is weakening as Amazon and Apple bid aggressively for live sports rights (NBA, MLS) and regional sports networks collapse (FanDuel Sports Network wound down May 2026); content IP (Marvel/Star Wars/Pixar) and a newly profitable streaming segment (10.6% operating margin) are the offsetting strength.

ECL.inst_own_summary: Fintel shows 74.91% institutional ownership with 12-month inflows of $8.54B versus $4.98B outflows (1,068 buyers vs 842 sellers); Vanguard is top holder.
ECL.moat_summary: Roughly 80% of revenue comes from an installed base of dispensers/dosing gear plus consumables (razor-and-blade), with revenue over twice its largest rival and ~9.5% of a $165B market; Morningstar rates it wide-moat.

ELV.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership about 89.24% with 1,591 holders; last quarter institutions bought 571.2K shares vs sold 375.7K, and some holders such as Corient trimmed.
ELV.moat_summary: BCBS licensee in 14 states plus 44.9M medical members and 90%+ group retention give scale and switching-cost advantages, though Carelon trails UnitedHealth's Optum in vertical integration.

EMR.inst_own_summary: Fintel shows 74.30% institutional ownership, with 12-month inflows of $11.87B (1,466 buyers) versus $5.52B outflows (1,224 sellers).
EMR.moat_summary: Deeply embedded DeltaV process-control systems and valve/instrumentation installed bases create high switching costs; GuruFocus moat score 7 and Morningstar wide moat, though Discrete Automation is more competitive.

EOG.inst_own_summary: Institutions hold ~89.9%; over 12 months 1,122 buyers vs 839 sellers but outflows ($7.38B) exceeded inflows ($6.60B).
EOG.moat_summary: GuruFocus scores EOG's moat 6 (narrow), built on a premium-well standard (60%+ after-tax return at conservative prices) and proprietary drilling and completion data, but with no regulatory barriers or unique IP.

EPD.inst_own_summary: Fintel-derived data shows only 21.51% institutional ownership because insiders hold 32.9% (Duncan family/affiliates) and many MLP units are held by retail; recent filings show BlackRock trimming 12.5% and small funds exiting.
EPD.moat_summary: Integrated NGL pipeline, storage and export network (50,000+ miles of pipeline) is described as wide-moat, with Q2 2026 network optimization capturing about $200M of incremental margin.

EQIX.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership is about 94.94% (2,262 holders); 886 buyers vs 617 sellers and $21.83B inflows vs $7.43B outflows over 12 months, with mixed individual filings.
EQIX.moat_summary: Interconnection ecosystem about twice the size of the next provider (GuruFocus moat score 8), though cloud on-ramp share reportedly fell from ~90% to 40-50%.

ETN.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership rose to 83.98% by July 2026 from 82.38% in August 2025 and 82.97% in October 2025, per GuruFocus.
ETN.moat_summary: Eaton sits at the physical bottleneck of AI data-center power delivery (grid-to-chip voltage conversion); Electrical Americas orders were up 60% YoY with data-center orders up 240%, a hard-to-replicate infrastructure position.

FDX.inst_own_summary: Institutions held about 81.4% as of June 2026 (up from 79.4%), with 904 funds adding vs 692 trimming and 8.7M net shares added QoQ.
FDX.moat_summary: Network-effect and scale advantages in express/freight (rated narrow moat by Morningstar-style views) but exposed to UPS/Amazon competition and volume softness.

FIX.inst_own_summary: MarketBeat shows 96.51% institutional ownership, with 578 buyers vs 336 sellers over 12 months and $4.73B inflows vs $2.53B outflows.
FIX.moat_summary: Alpha Spread rates it a narrow moat; few rivals can execute large complex mechanical/electrical data-center projects (technology now 56% of revenue) and its balance sheet and surety capacity are advantages, but barriers are limited outside specialized work.

FTNT.inst_own_summary: 65.2% institutional as of late July 2026, down from ~83.7% cited in a March 2026 report — sources disagree substantially on methodology, but the direction is consistently down across the year.
FTNT.moat_summary: FortiGate holds over 50% of the global network firewall market on a proprietary-silicon/hardware moat (1,280+ patents), but the industry's shift to cloud-native SASE/endpoint architectures is a named structural threat from Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike.

GE.inst_own_summary: 74.8% institutional per 2026 data (an earlier figure cited ~80%); no clear recent trend confirmed.
GE.moat_summary: GE holds roughly 70% of the narrow-body jet engine market in a structural duopoly with Pratt & Whitney/Rolls-Royce; its 40,000+ engine installed base locks airlines into multi-decade, high-margin aftermarket service contracts.

GEV.inst_own_summary: ~76% of shares outstanding held by 13F institutional filers as of Q1 2026 (3,062 institutional managers reported positions); Vanguard's stake was trimmed below the 5% disclosure threshold per a March 2026 13G/A amendment, a modest reduction rather than a broad trend.
GEV.moat_summary: GE Vernova holds a global 25-30% share in heavy-duty gas turbines off a ~7,000-unit installed base; once a utility commits to a GEV HA-class turbine it is effectively locked into a 20-30 year parts/service relationship.

GILD.inst_own_summary: Institutional investors control roughly 86% of Gilead shares, led by Capital Research (~11%), BlackRock (~9.7%) and Vanguard (~9.3%).
GILD.moat_summary: Biktarvy holds >52% share of the HIV treatment market and Descovy >45% of U.S. PrEP share; Biktarvy's U.S. patent exclusivity runs to 2036 and the new twice-yearly injectable lenacapavir (Yeztugo) further reinforces Gilead's HIV franchise lead.

GLW.inst_own_summary: 70.9% institutional as of July 21, 2026 per WallStreetZen (other trackers show 58-73%); Samsung Display is the single largest holder at 9.3%. No clear recent trend confirmed.
GLW.moat_summary: Rated a narrow (not wide) moat by analysts, but strengthening: Corning has signed multi-year, prepaid AI-fiber supply agreements with Meta (up to $6B), Amazon and Nvidia, evidence customers are paying up for capacity they see as hard to replace.

GOOG.inst_own_summary: 64.5% institutional per 2026 aggregated data (~8,008 institutional 13F/13D/G filers); figures are essentially identical to GOOGL since both are the same underlying company. Note: this is the Class C (no-vote) share class.
GOOG.moat_summary: Google's global search share fell below 90% for the first time in a decade (89.87%, down from ~91%) as ChatGPT Search, Perplexity, and other AI tools capture 15-20% of informational query volume, though Google retains dominance in navigational/transactional search plus Maps, YouTube and Android defaults.

GOOGL.inst_own_summary: 64.5% institutional per 2026 aggregated data (~8,008 institutional 13F/13D/G filers). GOOG and GOOGL are Alphabet's two share classes (Class C and Class A) — same company, same underlying ownership and moat picture.
GOOGL.moat_summary: Google's global search share fell below 90% for the first time in a decade (89.87%, down from ~91%) as ChatGPT Search, Perplexity, and other AI tools capture 15-20% of informational query volume, though Google retains dominance in navigational/transactional search plus Maps, YouTube and Android defaults.

GS.inst_own_summary: 70.8% institutional in March 2026, up marginally from 70.7% in December 2025 (essentially flat).
GS.moat_summary: Tier-1 advisory franchise and the integrated 'One Goldman Sachs' model (banking, markets, asset/wealth management) keep client switching costs high, but analysts note the firm's moat is 'narrower than it was' as trading/capital-markets businesses face rivals with larger, lower-cost balance sheets.

GWW.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership about 80.7% (72.8% at Dec 2025); shares held by institutions rose 5.07% QoQ with 843 buyers vs 653 sellers over 12 months.
GWW.moat_summary: Morningstar wide moat: high-single-digit share of fragmented North American MRO market with fast inventory turns and data/supply-chain advantages, with Amazon Business the main threat.

HCA.inst_own_summary: About 62.7% institutional ownership (Vanguard 9.2%, BlackRock 7.4%); over 12 months 882 buyers vs 693 sellers with $11.55B inflows vs $8.31B outflows.
HCA.moat_summary: Morningstar assigns a narrow moat: dense number-one/two hospital networks in Dallas, Houston and South Florida give scale purchasing and payer-negotiating leverage, but care is local, labor-intensive and payer-dependent.

HD.inst_own_summary: 73% institutional per an April 2025 report (a February 2026 source confirms it remains 'over 70%'); no precise recent trend figure found.
HD.moat_summary: 51% share of US home-improvement retail vs. Lowe's 28.8%, plus ~43% of online home-improvement sales vs. Lowe's ~21%; the SRS Distribution and GMS acquisitions expand Home Depot's addressable Pro-contractor market by roughly $50B.

HLT.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership about 96.36%, at or above free float, with Norges Bank opening a $695M stake though some small holders trimmed.
HLT.moat_summary: Wide moat from multi-brand global platform and loyalty program with asset-light fee model, though Hilton hotels do not show a systematic RevPAR premium over Marriott.

HON.inst_own_summary: MarketBeat shows 75.91% institutional ownership; over 12 months 1,897 buyers ($14.77B inflows) outweighed 1,565 sellers ($10.47B outflows), a 12-month rather than single-quarter measure.
HON.moat_summary: A large installed base of aerospace, building-automation and energy equipment drives aftermarket service revenue and high switching costs, with ROIC (10.5%) above WACC (7.2%).

HONA.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership not found: HONA only began trading June 29, 2026 after the Honeywell spin-off and searches returned no 13F ownership data.
HONA.moat_summary: Over $17B revenue, 36,000 employees and an installed base on virtually every commercial and defense aircraft platform, but no third-party moat rating found for the newly spun company.

HWM.inst_own_summary: Institutions and hedge funds own about 90.46% of HWM (1,524 institutional holders, ~375M shares); recent-quarter net direction not determined from results, with State Street reported adding shares.
HWM.moat_summary: Proprietary superalloy and casting know-how plus program-specific qualified tooling for jet-engine turbine blades create high switching costs and long-cycle OEM/aftermarket revenue.

IBKR.inst_own_summary: No clean 'institutional % of total shares' figure was found. Founder Thomas Peterffy controls ~76% of total voting power through IBG Holdings LLC, which alone holds ~73.5% of the company; the public float is only ~26.5% of shares outstanding, and institutional funds (Vanguard, BlackRock, State Street) dominate that smaller public float rather than the company as a whole — this is a controlling-insider situation, not a data gap.
IBKR.moat_summary: Automation-driven low-cost structure delivered a 79% pre-tax margin in Q4 2025; client equity reached ~$560B, up 28% YoY, letting IBKR spread fixed costs over a growing base in a way pricier full-service brokers can't easily match.

IBM.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership rose to 66.2% in June 2026 from 63.3% in March 2026; BlackRock is the top holder at 8.16%.
IBM.moat_summary: IBM holds a narrow moat (per AlphaSpread) built on high switching costs from complex enterprise integrations and OpenShift's hybrid-cloud differentiation vs. pure-public-cloud rivals AWS/Azure/GCP, aided by deep vertical expertise in regulated industries.

IDXX.inst_own_summary: Fintel shows 87.84% institutional ownership; 12-month inflows of $9.18B (865 buyers) versus $5.45B outflows (578 sellers), with big adds from BNY Mellon and Generation IM and a trim by First Trust.
IDXX.moat_summary: Installed base of over 142,000 in-clinic analyzers with over 90% recurring instrument-related revenue, high-90s customer retention and a reference-lab network against Antech (Mars) and Zoetis.

INTC.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership slipped to 68.4% in September 2025 from 68.9% in June 2025 per YCharts; BlackRock is the top holder at ~9.09%.
INTC.moat_summary: Intel's server CPU share fell to 54.9% in Q1 2026 from 64.4% a year earlier as AMD (+230bps to 27.4%) and Arm (+140bps to 17.7%) took share, and AMD's data-center revenue surpassed Intel's for the first time.

INTU.inst_own_summary: Fintel-type aggregator reported an implausible 125.7% institutional figure for Q1 2026 (short/derivative double counting), so no reliable percentage; BlackRock is top holder (~25.5M shares), 244 institutions opened and 481 exited positions in Q1 2026, NewEdge cut 27.1% in Q2, and Smart Money Score is 34/100 (bearish).
INTU.moat_summary: Moat not researched: the web search budget was exhausted before the Intuit moat query could run.

ISRG.inst_own_summary: 81.8% institutional as of September 2025, down from 84.4% in June 2025.
ISRG.moat_summary: Holds an estimated 70-80% share of soft-tissue robotic surgery (11,395 da Vinci systems installed, +12% YoY) with a moat reinforced by surgeon-training lock-in and 4,500+ patents; new entrants (Medtronic Hugo, J&J Ottava) are emerging but haven't yet dented share.

JNJ.inst_own_summary: 83.8% institutional per GuruFocus (June 2026); other trackers show a lower 70-74% range depending on date/methodology.
JNJ.moat_summary: Facing $4-4.5B of 2026 patent-cliff exposure (Stelara sales down 43% from biosimilar entrants), but J&J's MedTech arm (robotic-surgery entry via Ottava, hospital contract bundling) provides diversification pure-pharma rivals like Pfizer lack, and management still guides to >5% 2026 top-line growth.

JPM.inst_own_summary: 71.08% institutional ownership per Fintel; Vanguard Group is the largest holder at 9.53%.
JPM.moat_summary: Morningstar rates JPMorgan a Wide Moat; it holds top market share across global IB fees, institutional trading, domestic deposits, merchant acquiring, and credit card issuance, backed by switching costs and efficient scale.

KEYS.inst_own_summary: TradingKey shows institutional holding at 93.30%, up 1.34% quarter over quarter (other aggregators show ~85-89% due to differing methodology); no controlling insider stake.
KEYS.moat_summary: Keysight's 10-K says no competitor matches its breadth of proprietary test hardware and software across markets, and 2026 demand is supported by 6G digital-twin and PCIe 7.0 validation work.

KHC.inst_own_summary: Institutions hold about 78.2% (Berkshire Hathaway is the largest holder, about $7.3B at 3/31/26); over 12 months 741 buyers ($4.80B inflows) outweighed 574 sellers ($2.65B outflows), a 12-month rather than single-quarter measure.
KHC.moat_summary: Power Brands reach about 90% of US households and Morningstar rates the moat narrow, but three straight years of North America volume declines and private-label pressure point to erosion.

KKR.inst_own_summary: Institutions owned 73.2% as of June 2026, up from 70.4%; 669 of 1,344 holders added, 477 trimmed, with shares held up 5.35% QoQ (Norges Bank and Dodge & Cox top buyers).
KKR.moat_summary: Moderate moat from $724B AUM scale, LP relationship consolidation ('flight to quality'), and partnership-sourced deals, in an intensely competitive alternatives industry.

KLAC.inst_own_summary: 86.65% institutional ownership; trailing-12-month 13Fs show net institutional buying (~$13.2B inflows vs ~$8.9B outflows).
KLAC.moat_summary: KLA holds ~57% share in process-control/inspection segments with high switching costs from long equipment-qualification cycles, more than quadruple the share of its nearest rival Applied Materials in that niche.

KMI.inst_own_summary: Fintel shows 62.52% institutional ownership; 1,167 buyers vs 862 sellers over 12 months with $7.12B inflows vs $3.76B outflows (Vanguard 9.35%).
KMI.moat_summary: Hard-to-replicate natural gas pipeline network with take-or-pay contracts and rights-of-way; analysts split between narrow and wide moat due to modest returns on capital.

KO.inst_own_summary: 76.97% institutional ownership per Fintel (some sources show ~70%); Berkshire Hathaway remains the largest holder at 9.30%.
KO.moat_summary: Wide brand/distribution moat remains intact (20 consecutive quarters of value-share gains through 2026), but ~70% of revenue still comes from carbonated soft drinks, a category in structural decline in mature markets, creating slow erosion pressure.

LIN.inst_own_summary: 85% institutional ownership; top holders are Vanguard (6.54%), BlackRock (4.99%), and State Street (4.19%).
LIN.moat_summary: Linde's moat rests on irreplaceable on-site/pipeline infrastructure, inflation-indexed take-or-pay contracts, and route density (lowest per-delivery cost in its zip codes), a structural advantage over Air Products, its closest rival.

LLY.inst_own_summary: Estimates range widely by source (64%-92%); WallStreetZen cites 88.53% institutional, with Lilly Endowment (a large controlling foundation stake, not an index fund) holding ~10.1% as top shareholder.
LLY.moat_summary: Eli Lilly leads the US GLP-1 obesity/diabetes market with 60.1% share vs Novo Nordisk's 39.4%, and is extending the lead via a $6.5B API plant for its oral small-molecule GLP-1 (Foundayo), which is more scalable than Novo's peptide manufacturing.

LRCX.inst_own_summary: 84.61% institutional ownership; trailing-12-month 13Fs show strong net buying (~$57.1B inflows vs ~$5.0B outflows).
LRCX.moat_summary: Lam's etch/deposition tools carry high switching costs once qualified into a chipmaker's process node, and its large installed base drives high-margin recurring service revenue; it leads in etch/thin-film deposition though trails ASML/Applied Materials in overall WFE share.

MA.inst_own_summary: ~88% institutional ownership; Vanguard (8.6%) and BlackRock (7.7%) are the top holders per SEC filings.
MA.moat_summary: Mastercard's moat score of 9/10 reflects powerful two-sided network effects (9.1 sub-score), high switching costs for issuing banks, and regulatory licensing barriers across 210+ countries.

MAR.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership percentage and recent 13F change were not found in search results (only a generic HedgeFollow page surfaced); further searches were blocked by the search budget.
MAR.moat_summary: Moat rests on scale (largest global room count), 30+ brands and the Bonvoy loyalty network that makes franchise contracts sticky, though EcoMoat rates it only Moderate.

MCD.inst_own_summary: 75.30% institutional ownership; Vanguard is the largest holder at 10.15%.
MCD.moat_summary: McDonald's real-estate/franchise moat (46% operating margin) remains structurally intact against restaurant rivals, but GLP-1 drug adoption is reducing customer food consumption — a demand-side threat traditional competitive moats don't defend against.

MCHP.inst_own_summary: Institutions own about 91.51% (1,135 holders); 793 buyers vs 637 sellers but $8.70B inflows vs $20.85B outflows over 12 months.
MCHP.moat_summary: MPLAB X tooling and a 50,000+ SKU catalog lock in engineers on its microcontrollers, with cross-sold analog/power content and Microsemi-derived aerospace and defense positions.

MCO.inst_own_summary: MarketBeat shows 92.11% institutional ownership (Vanguard, TCI Fund, State Street largest); over 12 months 928 buyers ($10.37B inflows) outweighed 615 sellers ($8.64B outflows).
MCO.moat_summary: Morningstar wide moat: credit ratings are embedded in regulation, index rules and issuer relationships, so entrants face long certification hurdles against the Moody's/S&P duopoly.

META.moat_summary: Meta holds a Wide Moat rating with a Stable trend (moat score 8/10), driven by network effects across 3.54B daily active users and advertiser switching costs embedded in its ad platform.

MMM.inst_own_summary: Institutions held 75.2% as of June 2026 (up from 73.3% in March); shares held rose 2.98% QoQ with 908 institutions adding vs 840 reducing; BlackRock is largest at 8.67%.
MMM.moat_summary: Materials-science platforms (adhesives, abrasives, optical films) cross-sold across many end-markets are a real edge, but the PFAS manufacturing exit and litigation burden keep analysts split on moat strength.

MNST.inst_own_summary: Fintel shows 72.36% institutional ownership (638M shares); 12-month inflows of $8.44B versus $3.85B outflows, with MFS adding 9.35% while Janus Henderson cut about 42%.
MNST.moat_summary: Morningstar narrow moat built on brand and innovation plus the Coca-Cola distribution alliance (reinforced Dec 2025) spanning 200+ countries, against Red Bull, Coke and Pepsi.

MO.inst_own_summary: Fintel lists 2,528 institutional holders with about 1.18B shares, but no ownership percentage or recent-quarter net change was found in the results.
MO.moat_summary: Morningstar assigns a wide moat: Marlboro's US leadership, pricing power, and FDA/PMTA and MSA regulatory barriers keep new entrants out.

MPC.inst_own_summary: MarketBeat shows 76.77% institutional ownership; over 12 months 983 buyers ($9.03B inflows) outweighed 894 sellers ($6.18B outflows), a 12-month rather than single-quarter measure.
MPC.moat_summary: Morningstar keeps a narrow moat: as the largest US refiner (Marathon plus Andeavor), high-complexity Midcontinent and Gulf Coast plants get discounted crude, while West Coast assets are higher cost.

MPWR.inst_own_summary: MarketBeat shows 93.46% institutional ownership; 12-month inflows of $7.90B (710 buyers) exceed outflows of $4.82B (458 sellers), FMR holds 10.5%.
MPWR.moat_summary: Proprietary BCD process and 48V power IP with mid-50s gross margin support differentiation in AI servers, but Infineon and Renesas are reportedly winning share on NVIDIA Blackwell power.

MRK.inst_own_summary: ~79-83% institutional ownership depending on source/date; Macroaxis's more recent figure is 83%.
MRK.moat_summary: Keytruda (~40% of pharma revenue, ~$29.5B in 2024 sales) faces core US patent expiry in 2028, threatening up to 30% of total company revenue from biosimilar competition despite Merck's efforts to extend exclusivity via new formulations and follow-on patents.

MRVL.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership estimated 78.6%-83% depending on source; commonly cited figure is ~79.25%.
MRVL.moat_summary: Marvell's custom AI silicon (ASIC) business grew data-center revenue 42% YoY to ~$8.2B in fiscal 2026 via sticky hyperscaler design-in relationships (Amazon, Google, Microsoft), but it remains smaller and less diversified than chief rival Broadcom in custom silicon.

MS.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership estimates vary widely by source (59%-84%); most-cited figure is ~62.6%. Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group is the largest holder at 24.00%, a strategic partner stake rather than a typical index position.
MS.moat_summary: Morgan Stanley's wealth & asset management franchise (54% of net revenue, $9.3T in client assets) provides sticky recurring fee revenue, reinforced by its 'Morgan Stanley at Work' equity-plan platform that funnels future high-net-worth clients ahead of their IPOs.

MSFT.inst_own_summary: 81.55% institutional ownership as of July 2026 per GuruFocus (other sources show 66-74% depending on date/methodology); BlackRock is the largest holder (~$219.7B stake as of Q1 2026).
MSFT.moat_summary: Microsoft holds a Moat Score of 9/10 (#1 of 2,837 Software companies per GuruFocus), anchored by enterprise switching costs across Windows/Office/Azure and Azure's $75B+ annual revenue run-rate as the #2 global cloud provider.

MSI.inst_own_summary: MarketBeat shows 84.17% institutional ownership (other sources 86-91%) across ~1,450 holders led by Vanguard, Capital World and State Street; net trend not stated.
MSI.moat_summary: Wide moat from high switching costs in public-safety land mobile radio, video security and command-center software integrated into agency networks.

MSTR.inst_own_summary: Yahoo Finance shows about 61.9% institutional ownership (other sources 46-63%), with Vanguard the top holder at 8.99%; institutions bought 195.1M shares but sold 261.2M last quarter (net selling).
MSTR.moat_summary: No conventional operating moat; its edge is scale as the largest public bitcoin holder (about 66% of public-company bitcoin) and access to capital markets via preferreds, which depends on trading at a premium to NAV during a bitcoin drawdown.

MU.inst_own_summary: 84.44% institutional ownership as of June 2026 per GuruFocus.
MU.moat_summary: Micron narrowed the DRAM share gap with SK Hynix in Q2 2026 (Micron ~23-25% vs SK Hynix ~26%, Samsung ~39%) on HBM growth, but remains a distant third in HBM behind SK Hynix's dominant position with NVIDIA's flagship parts.

NBIS.inst_own_summary: Fintel shows 21.90% institutional ownership (119M shares, 752 holders); 12-month 232 buyers ($1.48B inflows) versus 45 sellers ($371M outflows), though low percentage reflects a large insider/founder stake.
NBIS.moat_summary: GPU-cloud moat rests on long-term power contracts in Finland and France and NVIDIA's roughly $2B investment for GPU priority, but GuruFocus scores moat 3 and capex needs are heavy.

NEE.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership estimates cluster around 85% (range ~79-87% across sources/quarters); Vanguard is the top holder at 10.34%.
NEE.moat_summary: NextEra's Florida Power & Light is the largest rate-regulated utility in Florida (~70% of NEE's earnings) operating in a constructive regulatory environment; the pending all-stock Dominion Energy acquisition would make NEE the world's largest regulated electric utility by market cap.

NEM.inst_own_summary: 82.37% institutional ownership as of Q1 2026 (879.38M shares, 3,100 institutions); inflows accelerated in early 2026 as hedge funds rotated from tech into 'real assets' like gold miners.
NEM.moat_summary: Newmont's moat comes from being the world's largest gold producer by scale/reserves, with copper byproduct credits lowering its all-in-sustaining costs, though as a commodity price-taker its moat is limited to cost-curve position rather than pricing power.

NFLX.inst_own_summary: 83.7% institutional ownership as of April 2026, up from ~82.1% in January 2026 - institutions have been piling in even as company executives head for the exits.
NFLX.moat_summary: Netflix remains the largest US streaming service (~27% share, 325M global subscribers), but its dominance is narrowing as Amazon Prime Video (~26%) and Disney+ grow, and YouTube increasingly dominates connected-TV viewing time.

NOW.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership fell to 83.4% in December 2025 from 90.4% in September 2025, per Business Quant.
NOW.moat_summary: ServiceNow's Now Assist AI product exceeded $600M in annual contract value in 2025 and is tracking toward $1B+ in 2026, deepening the platform's workflow-centrality and switching costs that underpin its moat.

NTRA.inst_own_summary: Fintel shows 99.90% institutional ownership but 12-month outflows of $14.04B exceeded inflows of $6.11B (467 buyers vs 292 sellers), so net institutional selling.
NTRA.moat_summary: MolDX Medicare coverage requires extensive clinical evidence Natera has built, plus MRD (Signatera) tech and a large genomic dataset, though ctDNA rivals and large labs are increasing competition.

NUE.inst_own_summary: MarketBeat shows 76.48% institutional ownership (TradingKey 79.13%, up 2.13% QoQ); BlackRock and BNY Mellon added big Q2 positions while Wellington cut 76.6%.
NUE.moat_summary: Largest US steelmaker (~25% of US capacity) with a decentralized profit-sharing non-union culture and high ROCE, but steel is price-competitive and some analysts see no formal moat.

NVDA.inst_own_summary: 67.36% institutional ownership as of Aug 27, 2026 per GuruFocus (range 54%-70% across sources/dates).
NVDA.moat_summary: NVIDIA holds ~75-81% of the AI accelerator market via its CUDA software moat (4M+ registered developers), but that moat is narrowing as open alternatives (Triton, PyTorch, ROCm 7) mature and hyperscaler custom ASIC shipments grow 44.6% YoY, nearly triple GPU growth.

NXPI.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership around 90.5-95.4% with 1,408 holders led by FMR at 9.99%; BlackRock added ~164K shares last quarter.
NXPI.moat_summary: Morningstar wide moat: long automotive design cycles, safety certification and deep customer integration create switching costs, while Infineon, Renesas and TI contest the same profit pool.

O.inst_own_summary: Institutions held 77.5% in Sept 2025 (down from 79.0% in June 2025); 736 of 1,307 filers increased and 401 reduced, so more buyers than sellers though total ownership slipped slightly (data is from the Sept 2025 quarter, not the latest).
O.moat_summary: Scale, an investment-grade balance sheet with low cost of capital, and proprietary deal flow from repeat corporate clients across ~15,600 net-lease properties (Walmart, FedEx) support accretive spreads, though growing competition for targeted assets may force more risk.

ORCL.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership has held in the 44-45% range through 2025 and into 2026 (44.10% in Q1 2026), with Vanguard (~6.02%) and BlackRock the largest holders.
ORCL.moat_summary: Morningstar downgraded Oracle's economic moat rating from wide to narrow, citing AI's potential to disrupt Oracle's traditional database/enterprise-software business even as its OCI cloud-infrastructure revenue grows fast (77% YoY in FY2026).

PANW.inst_own_summary: ~79.82% institutional ownership as of Q2 2026 (range 76.6%-80% across sources).
PANW.moat_summary: Palo Alto Networks captured the largest share of network-security market growth in 2024 (28.4%, outpacing rivals), with platform-consolidation switching costs ($1.2M-$3.5M migration cost vs $456K average contract) securing 85% of Fortune 100 as customers.

PAYX.inst_own_summary: Aggregator percentage was garbled in results so pct not recorded; March 2026 13Fs showed 716 holders adding vs 653 trimming and institutional shares up 84.8M QoQ.
PAYX.moat_summary: Morningstar wide moat from switching costs and compliance scale in SMB payroll (Paycor adds mid-market), but analysts flag AI commoditization risk to switching costs.

PDD.inst_own_summary: Only about 39.8% institutional ownership (ADS structure with a 927-holder base; founder/insider high-vote control likely explains the low figure); last quarter 262 institutions added vs 308 that cut.
PDD.moat_summary: Two-sided network effects and supply-chain scale in value commerce give it a narrow moat per most analysts, though heavy supply-chain investment and larger e-commerce rivals leave views split.

PEP.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership fell to 75.17% by August 2026 from 79.67% in Q1 2026; Vanguard (~10.1%) and BlackRock (~8.2%) are top holders.
PEP.moat_summary: PepsiCo carries a wide brand moat (GuruFocus moat score 8) but GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are flagged as a major structural risk to snack/soda volumes, with North American demand described in 2026 analyst commentary as 'fading.'

PFE.inst_own_summary: 66% institutional ownership as of Jan 2026; Vanguard (8.97%), BlackRock (7.70%), and State Street (5.10%) are top holders.
PFE.moat_summary: Pfizer faces $17-18B in annual revenue exposure from 2026-2028 patent expirations on blockbusters including Eliquis, Ibrance, and Xtandi, directly eroding its IP-based moat despite cost cuts and new oncology launches.

PG.inst_own_summary: About 66-69% of P&G shares are institutionally held (Vanguard ~9.6%, BlackRock ~6.8%, State Street ~4.4%), a level that has held fairly steady across recent quarters.
PG.moat_summary: P&G retains a Morningstar wide-moat rating on #1/#2 category-share brands (Tide, Pampers, Gillette) and >$8B annual ad spend, but recent growth has leaned on price hikes rather than volume, a flagged warning sign for pricing-power durability.

PLD.inst_own_summary: 92.83% institutional ownership per WallStreetZen (other sources cite up to 93.5%); Vanguard is the largest holder at 13.14%.
PLD.moat_summary: Prologis is the world's largest logistics REIT (~1.3B sq ft across 20 countries, ~20% share of key global distribution hubs), with scale-driven barriers to entry (5,500+ properties) sustaining 97%+ occupancy and 3-5% same-store NOI growth.

PLTR.inst_own_summary: 60.57% institutional per GuruFocus (Sep 2026), though HedgeFollow shows a much lower 45.65%; 13F data shows more institutional buyers than sellers by count but shrinking average position sizes last quarter.
PLTR.moat_summary: Morningstar-style coverage calls it a narrow-but-widening moat built on ~150% net dollar retention and deep government/defense integration, but the rise of agentic AI frameworks and rivals like Anthropic is specifically cited as beginning to erode that switching-cost advantage.

PM.inst_own_summary: ~84% institutional ownership as of 2026, up from 77% in an earlier-year reading, led by Capital Research and Vanguard.
PM.moat_summary: IQOS passed Marlboro as PMI's top nicotine brand by volume and hit a record 34.9% adjusted nicotine share in Q1 2026, with ~75% global category share in heat-not-burn.

PNC.inst_own_summary: About 76.8% institutionally held (insiders 0.30%); Fintel data shows institutions sold 316.6M shares versus 130.7M bought last quarter, i.e. net selling.
PNC.moat_summary: Morningstar gives PNC a narrow moat built on $560B+ of assets, regulatory barriers and sticky treasury-management relationships, though its deposit franchise carries no distinct cost edge over super-regional peers.

PSA.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership is about 78.79%, with 820 buyers vs 546 sellers and $7.95B inflows vs $4.42B outflows over the last 12 months.
PSA.moat_summary: Scale, brand and a 79% NOI margin via the PS Next online platform (70%+ leases online) plus the $10.5B National Storage Affiliates deal reinforce its lead, though Alpha Spread flags weak ROIC-based moat evidence.

PSX.inst_own_summary: Simply Wall St reports institutions holding roughly 72-80% of PSX across recent articles (Vanguard about 13%); no clear recent-quarter net flow found.
PSX.moat_summary: Integrated downstream mix of midstream, chemicals, refining and branded marketing gives diversification few pure-play refiners have, but it matches or trails some peers in scale.

PWR.inst_own_summary: Institutions own about 90.49% (TradingKey shows 95.28% with a -0.06% quarter-over-quarter change); Vanguard, BlackRock, State Street lead.
PWR.moat_summary: Largest skilled-lineman workforce in North America (owns Northwest Lineman College) plus patented energized-services methods and MSA lock-in with utilities; some analysts call the moat narrow rather than wide.

QCOM.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership was 78.38% as of August 2026 per WallStreetZen, up from ~74% cited in late November 2025.
QCOM.moat_summary: Qualcomm's smartphone chipset share fell from 27% (Q1 2025) to 23% (Q1 2026) as MediaTek grew to 32% share and Apple's in-house modem push cut Apple-related revenue sharply; Qualcomm is diversifying into automotive and data-center silicon to offset the decline.

RTX.inst_own_summary: 84.76% institutional as of April 2026 (GuruFocus), up from ~81% reported in January 2026.
RTX.moat_summary: Wide moat from patents, government contracts and a $86B defense backlog (Q2 2026), though Anduril is specifically named as an emerging threat in autonomous/AI battle-management systems.

SAP.inst_own_summary: US-listed ADR ownership data is inconsistent and not meaningful as a share of total SAP equity (Fintel lists 1,009 holders with 93.1M ADS; latest cycle 13 funds increased vs 15 reduced), so no reliable percentage was found.
SAP.moat_summary: SAP's moat rests on embedded ERP transactional data, process semantics and compliance controls for 400,000+ customers, with cloud revenue rising from EUR 8.7B (2021) to EUR 21.0B (2025) as AI is seen reinforcing rather than eroding lock-in.

SBUX.inst_own_summary: Fintel shows 72.29% institutional ownership; last 12 months had 1,593 buyers vs 1,497 sellers with $17.45B inflows vs $10.18B outflows.
SBUX.moat_summary: Brand and 35.5M-member Rewards program (57% of US sales) give pricing power, but Luckin passed it on store count and Dutch Bros beats its unit volumes.

SCCO.inst_own_summary: MarketBeat shows only 7.94% institutional ownership because parent Grupo Mexico controls roughly 89% of shares; over 12 months 470 buyers ($1.49B inflows) outweighed 271 sellers ($1.18B outflows).
SCCO.moat_summary: Large-scale, low-cost copper operations with very high-quality reserves (operating cash cost near $0.05/lb after by-products) give a cost moat, though Q2 2026 copper output fell 3.5% with Peru down 12%.

SCHW.inst_own_summary: 81.23% institutional as of August 2026 per GuruFocus, consistent with WallStreetZen's 81.11% in June 2026.
SCHW.moat_summary: Dominant in RIA custody with over 40% market share and $10T+ in client assets; integrated custody/banking/trading workflows create high switching costs for advisors.

SHOP.inst_own_summary: ~76% institutional as of July 2026, up from figures in the 65-68% range earlier in 2026 across multiple trackers.
SHOP.moat_summary: Shopify's share of top e-commerce sites grew from 18.5% to 26.9% over six years, directly taking share from Magento (down to 1.7%) as Adobe's enterprise pricing pushed SMBs to Shopify.

SHW.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership about 80.45% (81.6% mid-2025); Q2 activity mixed with State Street trimming 0.2% while Viking Global doubled its stake.
SHW.moat_summary: GuruFocus moat score 8: pricing power, 5,400+ company-operated stores selling exclusively branded products, and contractor color-matching and account tools raise switching costs.

SNDK.inst_own_summary: 76.85% institutional as of July 2026, down from 87.8% in Sept 2025 and 94.4% in June 2025 — a clear, sourced downward trend.
SNDK.moat_summary: SanDisk holds only ~13% of the NAND market (5th place) versus Samsung/SK Hynix/Micron/Kioxia; a dedicated 2026 moat analysis explicitly flags a declining moat despite BiCS8/9 technology gains.

SO.inst_own_summary: Institutional holders own about 70% (0.34% insiders) across 2,629 filers led by Vanguard 9.6%, BlackRock 7.9%, State Street 5.4%; a specific recent-quarter net flow was not found so trend is a stable-by-default judgment.
SO.moat_summary: Rate-regulated vertically integrated utility with 46 GW of regulated generation and 9M customers in fast-growing Southeast territories with data-center load growth.

SPCX.inst_own_summary: No usable post-IPO institutional-ownership percentage found after multiple queries (MarketBeat, Nasdaq, Fintel, Investing.com pages exist but did not return a figure); SpaceX listed June 12, 2026 with a 70:30 institutional:retail IPO allocation split, too recent for a 13F-based trend read.
SPCX.moat_summary: Falcon 9/Heavy carry ~85-90% of all payload mass launched to orbit globally, with SpaceX's share of the commercial launch market rising from ~60% (2025) to ~82% (March 2026); reusability and Starship give a widening cost advantage.

SPG.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership is about 93.01%, with 801 buyers vs 601 sellers and $10.57B inflows vs $4.33B outflows over the last 12 months.
SPG.moat_summary: Premium mall and outlet scale, 96% occupancy and an A credit rating support pricing power, though ROIC below WACC (2021-2025) tempers moat strength.

SPGI.inst_own_summary: As of Dec 2025, 2,112 institutions held 87.4% (down from 89.7% in Sep 2025) but total institutional shares rose 0.42% QoQ with 1,051 adding versus 789 cutting.
SPGI.moat_summary: Near-monopoly benchmarks in credit ratings, indexes and commodity pricing with regulatory barriers; GuruFocus moat score 8/10 and Morningstar wide moat.

SRE.inst_own_summary: MarketBeat puts institutional ownership at 89.65% (other sources 90-93.5%); recent-quarter net flow was not clearly reported, though Capital International disclosed a 3.0% stake.
SRE.moat_summary: Regulated monopoly utilities (SDG&E, SoCalGas, Oncor) plus long-term take-or-pay LNG export contracts (Cameron, Port Arthur) give a narrow, durable moat, with a $65B 2026-2030 capital plan.

STX.inst_own_summary: 87.55% institutional, down 8.75 percentage points quarter-over-quarter per mid-2026 data.
STX.moat_summary: Seagate leads Western Digital in HAMR deployment (Mozaic 3+ platform, 3TB+/platter density) and holds ~49% of the external-HDD segment, within a two-player HDD duopoly with high capital barriers to entry.

T.inst_own_summary: 57.10% institutional in Q3 2026, down from 66% reported in January 2026 — roughly a 9-point drop over the year.
T.moat_summary: AT&T's fiber footprint (38M+ locations, densest in the US, boosted by the Lumen Mass Markets acquisition) wins share from cable where deployed, but wireless remains highly competitive against T-Mobile and Verizon.

TER.inst_own_summary: Fintel shows 99.77% institutional ownership across 1,081 holders; recent filings mixed (ARK trimmed 3.09%, HOOPP added 44.83%), with 586 buyers vs 359 sellers over 12 months.
TER.moat_summary: Morningstar rates Teradyne wide-moat: a near-duopoly with Advantest in SoC test (about 40% share vs just over 50%), locked in by customers' custom code in its IG-XL software and the UltraFLEXplus platform's role in AI compute chip test.

TFC.inst_own_summary: Institutional holding about 85.71% (Q2 2026, up 10.2% QoQ per TradingKey) though Dec 2025 data showed 74.9% down from 77.2%; 808 funds added vs 616 cut.
TFC.moat_summary: Morningstar rates Truist no-moat; regional deposit franchise and treasury switching costs are moderate and trail JPMorgan and BofA in scale and fee breadth.

TGT.inst_own_summary: About 84% institutionally owned with Vanguard at 10%; recent 13F changes are small net adds (Vanguard +0.49% in the quarter) and no single holder has control.
TGT.moat_summary: Analyses say Target's moat is under pressure from a retail price war: Walmart reinvested about $2.9B of tariff refunds into 11,000+ price rollbacks while Target took its $994M to margin, and Costco's paid-membership loyalty is not matched by Target Circle.

TJX.inst_own_summary: 90.14% institutional per WallStreetZen (May 2026); one outlier source reported 31.46% but three other sources (94%, 90.14%, and share-count math) corroborate the ~90-94% range, so the low figure looks like a data anomaly.
TJX.moat_summary: Marmaxx (TJ Maxx/Marshalls/Sierra) captures roughly half of all US off-price retail sales; Morningstar explicitly rates TJX a wide moat anchored in global procurement scale that smaller off-price rivals like Ross and Burlington can't match.

TMO.inst_own_summary: 94.89% institutional as of August 2026, up from 89.23% reported mid-2026.
TMO.moat_summary: ~16% share of the life science tools market and the largest scale player; embedded service engineers and co-development partnerships with pharma/hospital customers create very high switching costs, with consumables/services now 78%+ of revenue.

TMUS.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership is about 41% of total shares; free float is constrained because Deutsche Telekom holds voting control of roughly 54.5% of outstanding stock.
TMUS.moat_summary: T-Mobile's network-performance lead (fastest 5G speeds and broadest coverage per Ookla/Opensignal) plus rapid Fixed Wireless Access broadband expansion continue to drive postpaid market-share gains over AT&T and Verizon.

TRI.inst_own_summary: Percentage not found on searched sources (only 8 13F filers listed on Fintel); Thomson family's Woodbridge controls roughly 70% of shares, so free-float institutional ownership is low.
TRI.moat_summary: Legal, tax and accounting products are embedded in workflows with 92% retention and duopoly positions in tax calculation, though AI raises competitive pressure.

TSLA.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership was 42.81% as of August 2026 per GuruFocus; Vanguard (~6.1%) and BlackRock (~5.0%) are the top holders.
TSLA.moat_summary: Tesla's U.S. EV market share dropped to 43.9% for full-year 2025 (its first time below 50%, down from ~80% in 2019) as deliveries fell 9% while the global EV market grew 26%, with Lucid and XPeng each posting triple-digit growth in competing segments.

TXN.inst_own_summary: 97.31% institutional as of June 2026 per GuruFocus; other 2025-era sources cited 87-88%, suggesting a rising or at minimum stably-high level.
TXN.moat_summary: TI holds ~19% of the global analog chip market (largest single share) and its $15B+ in owned 300mm fab capacity is called the strongest cost moat in analog semis, which no single competitor has matched.

UBER.inst_own_summary: 83.55% institutional as of April 2026 per GuruFocus, close to an 85.05% figure from another tracker — consistently in the low-to-mid 80s.
UBER.moat_summary: Uber holds ~76% of US rideshare vs Lyft's ~24%, but BofA projects that share slipping to ~73% by 2028 as Waymo, Tesla and Zoox autonomous fleets expand, even though Uber is positioning itself as the demand-aggregation layer those AV fleets plug into.

UNH.inst_own_summary: 87.86% institutional per recent 2026 tracking data; individual 13F activity is mixed, with some large holders (Norges Bank new position, Geode Capital +3.3%) adding even as the stock has sold off.
UNH.moat_summary: Regulatory scrutiny of prior authorization and Optum's PBM practices, plus a projected 1.3-1.4M Medicare Advantage member loss in 2026 and a ~40% YoY drop in 2025 operating earnings, is explicitly described by analysts as narrowing UNH's historically wide moat.

UNP.inst_own_summary: 83.47% institutional as of December 2025, consistent with an ~82% figure from another source around the same period.
UNP.moat_summary: Structural rail right-of-way barriers protect UNP's core position, and its pending Norfolk Southern combination would create the first US transcontinental railroad with >40% share of most commodity freight lanes, subject to a 2027 STB decision.

UPS.inst_own_summary: Institutions hold about 60.3% (some shares held by insiders/employees); 1,602 buyers vs 1,344 sellers over 12 months and several managers raised stakes (Van Eck +20.4%, Brighton Jones +63.8%) in recent quarters.
UPS.moat_summary: Morningstar gives UPS a wide moat built on an irreplicable network of 500+ aircraft, 100,000+ vehicles and hundreds of hubs moving about 22M packages a day, plus integrated-logistics switching costs.

URI.inst_own_summary: Fintel shows 96.26% institutional ownership; 12-month 993 buyers ($11.06B inflows) versus 660 sellers ($8.15B outflows), including Norges Bank's new $695.7M Q4 position.
URI.moat_summary: Narrow moat from largest rental fleet purchasing scale, dense branch network and seven specialty units (power, infrastructure) that add resilience versus smaller rivals.

V.inst_own_summary: 77.24% institutional currently, with other 2026 readings ranging 74.8%-83.8% depending on date/methodology — no clear directional trend, best read as stable in the high-70s to low-80s.
V.moat_summary: Network effects across 130M+ merchant locations underpin a wide moat; rather than being disrupted by stablecoins, Visa launched its own Visa Stablecoin Platform and is already processing $3.7B in stablecoin-linked card volume, turning a potential threat into a product line.

VLO.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership about 78.69% (other sources 85-87%), Vanguard holds 12.18%; 12-month inflows of $8.59B (1,019 buyers) exceed outflows of $5.05B (807 sellers).
VLO.moat_summary: Second-largest independent US refiner (~3M bpd) with complex refineries running discounted heavy/sour crude and owned logistics, but it is a commodity processor exposed to crack spreads.

VRTX.inst_own_summary: 93.79% institutional per WallStreetZen 2026 data; no reliable prior-period figure was found to establish a trend direction.
VRTX.moat_summary: Near-monopoly in cystic fibrosis with Trikafta/Alyftrek covering 95% of US CF patients and >40% operating margins, though Sionna Therapeutics' NBD1 stabilizers and Krystal Biotech's KB407 are named as the first credible emerging threats to that dominance.

VZ.inst_own_summary: Institutional ownership estimates cluster in the low-to-high 60s (63.5%-69.7% depending on source/quarter); Vanguard, BlackRock and State Street are the top three holders.
VZ.moat_summary: Verizon holds a Morningstar narrow moat but has been steadily losing postpaid wireless share to T-Mobile and AT&T -- one analysis cites a roughly 30% share decline over eight years -- after 5G network investment leveled the playing field among all three major carriers.

WBD.inst_own_summary: MarketBeat lists 59.95% institutional ownership (dated ~Oct 2025); other trackers show 68-74%, and recent-quarter net buying/selling was not found in results (deal/takeover activity muddies 13F flows).
WBD.moat_summary: GuruFocus moat score of 6 (narrow at best) and Alpha Spread says no economic moat, as linear networks (TNT, CNN, Discovery) decline against Netflix/Disney streaming competition despite HBO and Warner Bros. studio franchises.

WDC.inst_own_summary: 95.03% institutional as of June 2026, up slightly from ~92.5% in April 2026.
WDC.moat_summary: Now a pure-play HDD company post-SanDisk spin-off, WDC holds ~40-41% of the HDD market in a duopoly with Seagate; its entire 2026 HDD production capacity is sold out with supply contracts extending to 2027-2028.

WELL.inst_own_summary: WallStreetZen shows Welltower institutional ownership at 96.09%, with Vanguard the top holder at ~15.5%.
WELL.moat_summary: Welltower's proprietary data/tech platform compresses senior-housing deal diligence to 30 days vs. 5-10 months industry-standard, and SHOP occupancy rose to 87.3% in Q1 2026 from 85.1% a year earlier, reinforcing its operating-scale advantage.

WFC.inst_own_summary: 79.64% institutional as of July 31, 2026, a quarter-over-quarter decrease of 0.91 points.
WFC.moat_summary: The Fed's 2025 removal of Wells Fargo's $1.95T asset cap (in place since the 2018 fake-accounts scandal) restores its ability to compete on scale after 7 constrained years; its low-cost deposit base and Western/Southern US brand remain intact underlying advantages.

WMT.inst_own_summary: Q1 2026 13F data show institutional ownership at 35.9% (4,337 institutions), up ~3.66 points QoQ; the Walton family separately controls ~45% of shares as insiders, which caps the institutional share below typical mega-cap levels.
WMT.moat_summary: Walmart holds a Morningstar wide-moat rating (GuruFocus moat score 8-9) backed by roughly two-thirds share of the U.S. superstore/warehouse-club market and a leading ~31% online grocery share, driven by scale-based cost leadership.

XOM.inst_own_summary: 66.61% institutional per WallStreetZen (Aug 2026), down from a 76.71% GuruFocus reading in June 2026 — likely partly methodology-driven, so treat the drop's exact size with caution.
XOM.moat_summary: Lowest-cost-producer moat backed by $15.6B in cumulative structural cost savings since 2019 and a Permian asset base with double the low-cost drilling locations of its nearest competitor; advantaged-barrel mix (Permian/Guyana/LNG) rose from 52% to 59% of production.
